claim: `tprod_nonneg` assumes `[L.NeBot]`, which the statement does not need: when `L` is not `NeBot`, `tprod_bot` turns `∏'[L] i, f i` into `∏ᶠ i, f i`, and that is nonnegative too. The sibling lemmas in this file, `one_le_tprod` (whose additive form is `tsum_nonneg`) and `tprod_le_one`, already handle the `¬ L.NeBot` case this way and carry no `NeBot` assumption. As written, the new lemma is strictly weaker than its siblings for an arbitrary summation filter.
requested_change:
Drop `[L.NeBot]` from `tprod_nonneg`. Handle the degenerate filter the way `one_le_tprod` and `tprod_le_one` do: split on `L.NeBot`, and in the `¬ L.NeBot` branch use `rw [tprod_bot hL]; exact finprod_induction (0 ≤ ·) zero_le_one (fun _ _ ↦ mul_nonneg) hf`. (`finprod_nonneg` itself needs `CommSemiring` and `IsOrderedRing`, so it is too strong for these typeclasses.) Verified replacement:
theorem tprod_nonneg [CommMonoidWithZero α] [TopologicalSpace α] [Preorder α] [ZeroLEOneClass α]
    [PosMulMono α] [ClosedIciTopology α] {f : ι → α} (hf : ∀ i, 0 ≤ f i) :
    0 ≤ ∏'[L] i, f i := by
  by_cases hL : L.NeBot
  · by_cases h : Multipliable f L
    · exact le_hasProd_of_le_prod h.hasProd fun s ↦ s.prod_nonneg fun i _ ↦ hf i
    · simp [tprod_eq_one_of_not_multipliable h]
  · rw [tprod_bot hL]
    exact finprod_induction (0 ≤ ·) zero_le_one (fun _ _ ↦ mul_nonneg) hf
